result.summary: Adds a small CloseLogFile() helper in src/logging.cpp that checks fclose() return values and reports failures (with path and errno) directly to stderr, applied consistently at shutdown, log-file reopen, and shrink/rotate call sites. No behavior change is intended on the success path; only failure reporting is added.
result.problem: Some fclose() calls in logging.cpp previously ignored the return value, so a write-back error (e.g. disk full) on log file close could go unnoticed, silently losing log lines or misleading users into thinking rotation/truncation succeeded. This mainly affects node operators trying to diagnose issues via debug.log during disk problems.

result.card: This PR adds a helper to check fclose() return values in src/logging.cpp and report failures (with errno) to stderr at shutdown, log-file reopen, and log shrink/rotate, so that write errors on the debug log (e.g. disk full) are no longer silently swallowed. The commit message states the motivation: 'Several fclose() calls in src/logging.cpp ignored the return value which can risk silent loss of log lines or misleading success during rotate/truncate.' Review has been active across several rounds (ajtowns, maflcko, sedited) with no objection to the approach, only style and scope nits, most resolved in the 2026-07-28 push; a fresh round of minor nits and a question about a stale commit message from sedited (2026-09-08) remains unanswered past the waiting-on-author threshold. The change is narrow in scope (utils/logging only) and defensive rather than fixing an observed incident. It conflicts with two open logging-related PRs (#36197, #30342) that may require rebasing.
